Check keys of linked tables

check_keys.Rd

Data quality check before profile_data(): are key columns present and complete, is the main table unique on its key, and do the other tables only refer to persons in the main table? Persons who are missing from a linked table (no contacts, no admissions) are normal and not reported.

Usage

check_keys(tables, keys, main = NULL, config = NULL, target = "keys")

Arguments

tables

A named list of data frames.

keys

Key column. Either one name used in every table, or a named character vector mapping table names to key columns, for example c(persons = "person_id", contacts = "pid").

main

Name of the table with one row per person. By default the first table whose key is unique.

config

A mimic_config(); NULL uses the defaults.

target

Label used in reports.

Value

A mimic_check. Missing keys and duplicates in the main table fail; rows that refer to unknown persons give a warning.

See also

Other checks: check_differencing(), check_dominance(), check_extremes(), check_group_disclosure(), check_k_anonymity(), check_min_count(), check_model(), check_suppression()

Examples

check_keys(list(persons = fake_persons, contacts = fake_contacts,
                admissions = fake_admissions),
           keys = "person_id")
#> ✔ keys (keys): Keys are complete and all linked tables refer to persons in 'persons'.
